kQ5d41kEDQDwVqg1LWVYuK.description: Nancy approached the old house above the lake, not knowing quite what to expect. "The address is right," she told herself.  "but how long has this place been sitting here?  Since the horse and buggy days?" Up the stairs to the huge covered, she tried the door.  And it was open!  She went in and was amazed to see how houses actually looked in 1904.  Paneled walls, beamed ceilings, leaded, bevel edge glass windows, stained glass and the old country kitchen ahead in the next room.  But it was the garret she was most interested in.  She took out her flashlight and made her way slowly up the dark stairs, step by step, until she was at the landing.  The door was open!  Stepping into the room she found the light switch and turned it on.  What presented itself to her eyes was nothing short of a revelation.  Slanted, ceilings, beams, alcoves and furnishings, including a four poster bed straight out of a Victorian fantasy novel. "So this is it.  This is where I'm going to live." $745 later she was, indeed, living there, the most intriguingly magical place she had ever known. G&G, from high above the shores of Lake Union
kQ5d41kEDQDwVqg1LWVYuK.title: Nancy Drew and the Hidden Staircase

I have a full-time job that keeps me very busy. I will not rent this room to anyone who is a hardcore drug user, sex offender, or a felon due to the sensitivity and nature of my occupation. I prefer to rent to those who are social and not hide in their rooms until the sun sets.  I live to entertain my friends so they will be over from time to time to play boardgames, D&D, Magic the Gathering, and tabletop miniature games.  I do play on the PS5 and Switch from time to time when not entertaining.  When I am not gaming, I partake in some athletic sports or painting miniatures.  I am very cool, laidback, and a non-drama kind of guy.  I do chill from time to time and binge watch in the living room. Understanding that the times are tough as far as rent is concerned, credit checks, and whatnot, there is no deposit for rent.  Being that I have one dog at my residence, I cannot accept any other pets at this time.  My dog is not cat friendly whatsoever due to a stray cat who constantly torments them. The room is furnished and comes with a huge futon bed, a 70" Smart TV, 4k Blu-ray player, and a PS4.  If you want all of that removed, that could be accommodated.  The room is on the 2nd floor and that would require someone who is ambulatory to climb them.  There is a washer and dryer in the basement for your use.  the kitchen and living room are free to be used.  Respect my property if you use it. tYQUmMVhKVe7GuLRFizeS8.description: Classic Ballard character meets an unbeatable location! This spacious 500 sq. ft. studio offers the charm and character you just don't get in newer apartment buildings. Enjoy beautiful hardwood floors, high ceilings, and a huge closet with plenty of room for storage. The kitchen includes a full-size oven, and the building offers convenient on-site laundry. Residents also have access to a shared courtyard, a great spot to enjoy some fresh air or relax outside. Note: Pictures are of similar apartments in building. Apartment Features Approximately 500 sq. ft. Hardwood floors High ceilings Huge walk-in-style closet with excellent storage Full-size oven Pet friendly Laundry in the building Common courtyard Classic building with vintage Ballard charm Live in the Heart of Ballard The location is hard to beat — you're just 2 blocks from the Ballard Sunday Farmers Market, where Ballard Avenue comes alive every Sunday with local farmers, food vendors, baked goods, flowers, and artisan products. Ballard Farmers Market Step outside and you're surrounded by independent restaurants, coffee shops, boutiques, bars and breweries. Ballard's brewery district features more than a dozen breweries and cideries within about a mile. 44kY3G2tWw833sk4spVKY5.description: Hi all, I’m looking for someone interested in renting a room in a nice craftsman house at the top of Queen Anne. I’ve had good luck with housemates in the past, with many staying good friends afterward. So it probably makes sense to share a bit about me and the other housemate so we can explore if it might be a good fit. I’m a 54 year old male tech worker who is a bit of an extroverted introvert — meaning I enjoy having people over and entertaining, but also enjoy my quiet time. Love cooking, wine and cocktails, as well as movies and good TV shows, and host semi-regular weekly social dinner parties/get togethers to watch with friends. Have a friendly four year old German Shepherd, as well as housesit/care for two a couple of other friends’ dogs on and off. They all have full access to the fenced in yard and house through a dog door, so you’d need to be comfortable with having animals lounging around most of the time. I have one other housemate who currently lives here, and he’ll be available to meet and chat about living here as well. I’m the homeowner, and hope to find someone who enjoys living in the house, is comfortable hanging out in the living room or cooking in the kitchen (if they want), and doesn't feel as though they need to just hide in their room (unless you want quiet time of course). We are both pretty clean, and keep the house in that vein as well with several robot vacuums fighting the ever-present doghair battle. Kitchen is newly remodeled and fully stocked if you enjoy cooking. The house is a block from Queen Anne Avenue and Trader Joes and the new Safeway. The area has easy bus transit and driving access to downtown, and includes a two car driveway (a rarity up here!) Though the ad is for a private bedroom, it's really for living in a full two-story Queen Anne craftsman with finished basement, some off street parking, and some garage storage. I say semi-furnished in the headline because there are a variety of options here — I have a new Queen sized bed and mattress that can be made available, or you can bring your own things. There are two bathrooms (both shared but well maintained), in-house basement laundry and high speed internet (wired/Wifi) with free access to most streaming services is also available (Netflix, HBO, Amazon). The room is currently an office (pictures are from previous tenants), but can easily be freed up within a few days. If interested, there will be a standard rental agreement and one month rent deposit, as well as an applicant paid renter background check (yes, there’s a story there). However, happy to meet first to give you a chance to see the place and see if it makes sense to proceed. Utilities are shared equally across all roommates, with full bill availability/disclosure. For context, Seattle utilities are stupidly expensive, and some bills come every two months — so the total stack tends to jump from low one month to being high the next. A reasonable blended monthly average with three people is probably around $200. Again, the bills are fully transparent and available, no sketchy mystery fees here. Any questions, please drop me a line and thanks for reading! Obligatory tourist details: Queen Anne is known for sweeping vistas, tree lined streets and rolling landscapes. With its iconic coffee houses, the local family friendly business district is home to countless shops, restaurants, and specialty gift stores. You don't have to leave this neighborhood to find some of the city's best dining options with a variety of restaurants that serve Italian, Cuban, Mexican, Vietnamese, Japanese, Thai, French, Seafood, Vegetarian and American dishes.

crPdjKkxXD2QoeCWmpNPuh.description: Tired of cramped rentals, random roommate roulette, and trying to build a real life in a place that feels temporary? This is the opposite. A room is opening in our Sammamish home on 2 acres in the heart of the city. We’re looking for one great fit to join the house. The vibe is clean, quiet, respectful, and high-functioning. The tenant base is also very stable: everyone is on 12-month leases, and renewals are common, so this is not a high-churn roommate setup. Current housemates are working professionals in the software and aerospace industries. The house is quiet, respectful, and very stable. If you’re looking for a calm, well-run home with thoughtful working professionals, this will probably feel like a strong fit. What makes this place different is that it gives you something that is genuinely hard to find on the Eastside: real space, real privacy, and real access to daily life without feeling isolated. You’re in the heart of Sammamish — repeatedly rated one of the best small cities in Washington — but the property itself feels tucked away and deeply Pacific Northwest. It sits on 2 acres, with a seasonal creek, botanical-garden feel, huge windows looking out over a redwood grove, and a steady wildlife show from spring through fall. You can walk to the lake, groceries, banks, restaurants, gyms, and yoga, so this is one of those rare setups where nature and convenience are both right outside your door. The location is strong for commuting too. Highland Sammamish Plaza is within walking distance, and Metropolitan Market is about 2 minutes away. You’re about 5 minutes from the nearest beach and multiple city parks, around 10 minutes to Whole Foods, Costco, Redmond Town Center, Amazon Redmond, and SpaceX, around 15 minutes to Microsoft, T-Mobile, and Costco HQ, and about 20 minutes to Amazon Bellevue and Google Kirkland. The room itself is one of the standout features here. It’s an XL bedroom with a private patio — about 400 square feet for the room itself, plus roughly another 500 square feet of private outdoor patio space. It feels more like a private suite than a typical bedroom rental, with big built-in closets and enough space to actually live in, not just sleep in. It can also come furnished, and the listing photos show the kind of furnished setup available. You also get access to a large shared deck and your own full-size fridge in the kitchen. The house includes a designer kitchen with a JennAir gas range, Thermador convection oven, and Miele dishwasher, plus a high-end Samsung washer, Maytag dryer/steamer, and instant hot water for effectively endless showers. Monthly rent is $1,600 + 1/3 of trailing 12-month average household running costs. That covers your share of utilities (water, sewer, garbage, electricity, gas), high-speed internet, and professional landscaping. This is a strong fit for someone who is clean, considerate, and looking for a calm, quiet, non-party home. It’s a good fit for someone who values peace, privacy, and a beautiful setting — and contributes to that kind of environment. If that sounds like you, reach out and tell us a bit about yourself, what you do, and what kind of living environment you’re looking for. Please include your email in your message. Chinatown, which is located on the southeast side of downtown, is part of the International District, along with Japantown and Little Saigon. It is one of Seattle's eight historic neighborhoods, dating back to the mid-1800s. aoxRJQLCPjuNVNvg6Fmthz.description: We have two bedrooms opening up in our four-bedroom home in North Greenwood, available October 1st and November 1st. Rent is $1,000/month + $125/month for utilities, which includes Wi-Fi. The house has been fully remodeled over the past ten years with high-quality finishes, lots of natural light, and a comfortable, lived-in feel. Both available bedrooms are on the main level and share a bathroom with each other. The other two bedrooms each have their own private bathroom. The available rooms are approximately 10’ x 8’ and can comfortably fit a queen-size bed. Both have closets, multiple functional windows, and privacy with views toward the garden. The house The common areas are already furnished, and the kitchen is large with plenty of storage. Everyone has their own pantry/cupboard space, and there are already plenty of kitchen supplies, so you won’t need to show up with an entire kitchen’s worth of stuff. There’s also a large shared backyard that is maintained by the owner. The property includes a separate backyard cottage where two additional friends live, and we all share the yard. The house is in a quiet residential neighborhood with the Interurban Bike Trail right nearby, making it easy to bike around North Seattle. There’s also easy access to public transportation, including buses and the Northgate Link light rail station. There’s plenty of street parking in the area, and laundry is available in the home. What it’s like living here The four of us currently living between the main house and cottage have been friends for a long time, and we’re excited to welcome some new people into the mix. We’re all 25–28 and work typical 9–5 jobs, so the house tends to be pretty relaxed during the week. We’re a pretty social household—we like to hang out together on weekends, whether that’s watching sports, having people over, going out, or just hanging in the backyard—but we’re also pretty independent during the week and everyone has their own schedules and lives. Between us, our interests include sports, camping, art, and music festivals. Keeping the house clean is important to us. We don’t have a strict chore schedule, but everyone contributes and helps keep the common areas clean and in good shape. Guests are welcome, and we’re currently a no-pets household. A few of us smoke occasionally, but never inside the house, so there are no indoor smoking odors. Overall, we’re looking for people who are friendly, respectful, reasonably clean, and interested in being part of a good household dynamic. Also let us know whether you’re interested in a 6- or 12-month lease. We’re looking forward to meeting some new people and finding a good fit for the house!
